analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן introduces the naming of Babel. The following כִּי clause gives the reason for the name: YHWH confused the language of the whole earth there.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition governing כֵּן, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עַל כֵּן introduces the naming of Babel. The following clause, כִּי שָׁם בָּלַל יַהְוֶה, gives the reason for the name by linking בָּבֶל with בָּלַל, ‘he confused.’
analysis.morphology: An uninflected demonstrative particle used adverbially with the preceding preposition עַל.

analysis.evidence: In קָרָא שְׁמָהּ בָּבֶל, שְׁמָהּ means “its name” and בָּבֶל gives the name assigned to the city.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason for the name בָּבֶל. The following clause says that there (שָׁם) YHWH confused (בָּלַל) the language of the whole earth.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
